description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Build and evaluate robotic systems for complex maintenance work in service environments. This role combines hardware integration, teleoperation, and experimental validation to identify and address the barriers to reliable robot performance.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Diagnose robot capabilities and limitations in service bay conditions, identifying hardware and software bottlenecks.

 - Design and build teleoperation rigs that integrate robot arms, end effectors, cameras, and VR or leader-follower control systems.

 - Break complex repair tasks into testable subtasks and validate robot performance on each.

 - Investigate failures involving operator visibility, control latency, perception, motion control, reach, and dexterity.

 - Run controlled experiments on force feedback, force and torque sensing, compliant control, and tooling improvements.

 - Analyze completion rates, cycle times, and human interventions, and record synchronized sensor data for learning algorithms.

 - Move validated tasks from bench experiments to supervised trials in service environments.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging physical robots.

 - Experience in robotic manipulation or teleoperation, with proficiency in C++, Python, and ROS 2 or equivalent frameworks.

 - Experience designing experiments that distinguish software limitations from hardware constraints.

 - Experience testing or operating robots with safety procedures around people and vehicles.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary: $205,000 to $305,000 annually, plus stock options. Visa sponsorship is not available.


LOCATION

On-site in San Francisco, California, United States.
